children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares fell on Monday as chipmakers slid ahead of Nvidia earnings later this week, a key test of investor appetite for the artificial intelligence trade. The won strengthened, while the benchmark bond yield rose.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was down 93.07 points, or 1.76%, at 5,197.46, as of 0112 GMT.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
fell 1.82%, while peer SK Hynix
lost 3.95%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 1.85%, while Hyundai Motor
was unchanged and sister automaker Kia Corp
rose 0.42%.

** SK Hynix said it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market.
** Jensen Huang is considering ​a comeback as Nvidia's
chief executive, and ‌has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar ​with the matter.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 2.91%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
was flat.
** Of the total 909 traded issues, 214 shares advanced, while 664 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 570.7 billion won.
** The won was quoted at 1,333.8 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.28% higher than its previous close at 1,337.6.
** The KOSPI has risen 23.33% so far this year.
** The won has strengthened 7.9% against the dollar this year.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on 3-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.02 point to 103.40.
** The most-liquid 3-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 1.2 basis points to 3.768%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
rose by 1.5 basis points to 4.002%.
